hypotheses.construction_plan: Take the binary kernel K[θ1, θ2] = T(θ1, θ2). The two observed members are the two orbit representatives obtained by the slot permutation σ: σ·K[θ1, θ2] = K[θ2, θ1]. Thus the shared structure is the unordered orbit of the kernel under slot swap, with the two members recovered by choosing the two slot orders.
required_assumptions: T is a binary function with two ordered slots
slot permutation σ is a well-defined involution on this family
hypotheses.rationale: The two non-identical members are related by reversing the order of arguments of the same binary T. This is structurally an S2 orbit of a binary slot kernel, so a single symmetry-invariant object with a permutation operator explains both members.
